findings.title: Salesforce: undeclared prisma, and token refresh runs on every client construction
findings.body:
`prisma` is used at line 96 but never imported in this file, so this fails to compile or throws at runtime. The new refresh block also runs on every client construction, without checking expiry. It never calls `refreshOAuthTokens`, so credential sync is bypassed here. The jsforce Connection at lines 101-108 is still built from the old `credentialKey.access_token`, so the freshly fetched token is discarded.

A failed refresh now breaks the whole service, and a successful one adds a network call to every instantiation.

findings.title: Computed zod keys are bogus, so the minimal schema is wrong
findings.body: `[z.string().toString()]` evaluates to the string "[object Object]" or similar. The schema therefore requires a numeric property with that literal name, so `safeParse` fails on real token responses whenever credential sync is on. Zod objects strip unknown keys by default, so data such as `expiry_date` or `refresh_token` is dropped. The intended 'any number is the expiry' logic does not exist; it needs `.passthrough()` or `catchall`.

findings.title: Placeholder refresh_token written for schemas that don't define it
findings.body: Setting `refresh_token = "refresh_token"` as a fake value mutates the parsed data for every caller, even with sharing disabled. For Google, Office365 and Salesforce it injects a bogus refresh token into stored credentials. This is also a TypeScript error, because `data.refresh_token` does not exist on the type for schemas that lack it.

findings.title: parseRefreshTokenResponse result stored as the key
findings.body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns a safeParse result object (`{success, data}`), not the data. It is saved directly as `key`, so the stored credential becomes `{success:true,data:{...}}`. This corrupts Google credentials and breaks all subsequent auth. It should use `.data`.

findings.title: Sync endpoint call is unauthenticated and unchecked
findings.body: The POST to the credential-sync endpoint sends no secret or auth header, so the endpoint cannot verify the caller. The response status is never checked before callers parse it. Callers expect different shapes (axios `.data`, a fetch Response, or Google `.res`) from the sync endpoint's plain fetch Response. For example, zoho `tokenInfo.data` and the Google `res?.data` access are undefined on a fetch Response.

findings.title: Secret compared non-constant-time; unvalidated input and decrypt errors
findings.body: The header secret is compared with `!==`, which is not timing-safe. `parse` throws a ZodError (500) on a bad body instead of a 400. The JSON.parse and decrypt calls are also unguarded, so malformed payloads return 500s. The route accepts any method.

findings.title: Non-boolean flag exported
findings.body: `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is a `string | undefined` (the secret itself) rather than a boolean. It is easy to misuse or leak, so wrap it in `!!(...)`.

findings.title: Synced response not normalized
findings.body: With sync enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a raw fetch Response. It is treated as a HubspotToken, so `expiresIn` and `accessToken` are undefined. `setAccessToken(undefined)` is then called and garbage is saved to the credential. The same pattern applies to the zoho-bigin and zohocrm `.data` accesses.
